advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an assertion that the unmounted-scratch refusal carries its distinct operator message / scratch_unavailable coverage detail, distinguishing it from the plain free-space low-disk refusal.
evidence: src/rebar/review_bot/low_disk.py:100-116 scratch_unavailable_decision emits a distinct message containing 'not mounted' and the detail, plus coverage_gap/gap_reason

Absence rationale: search of tests for 'scratch_detail' and 'scratch_unavailable' returns only the AC5 patch-sentinel test; no assertion on the refusal message or the scratch_unavailable/scratch_detail coverage fields

Named violating input: with declaration present + proof absent, if pre_clone_refusal returned low_disk.decision() (the plain free-space refusal) instead of scratch_unavailable_decision(detail), every scratch test would still pass because status and gap_reason are identical, yet the operator-facing sub-condition the module docstring calls load-bearing ('carried in the coverage block and the operator-facing message, where it informs') would be silently lost
advisory.finding: The newly added scratch-unavailable refusal output (the distinct operator message 'declares a dedicated gate-scratch volume that is not mounted' and the coverage-block fields scratch_unavailable / scratch_detail) is never asserted by any test. All scratch tests assert only res['status']=='deferred' and res['gap_reason']=='low-disk', which the pre-existing free-space decision() also produces, so nothing distinguishes the two refusal shapes.
scenarios: A refactor collapses pre_clone_refusal to a single generic low-disk decision, dropping the mount-specific operator message and scratch_detail; the suite stays green while operators lose the reason the clone was refused
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_unmounted_scratch_refuses_the_review_bot_clone, additionally assert the refusal is the scratch-specific shape, e.g. assert 'not mounted' in res['message'] (or assert res['verdict']['coverage']['scratch_unavailable'] is True and res['verdict']['coverage']['scratch_detail'] mentions the marker), so the mount-specific branch is distinguished from low_disk.decision().
